title: lightseekorg/tokenspeed agentic inference engine and scheduler FSM mechanisms
observations: TokenSpeed separates the control plane (C++ FSM with compile-time type safety) from the execution plane (Python), enforcing request lifecycle and KV cache invariants via the type system.
Overlap scheduling with in_flight_depth and results_in_flight counters hides CPU scheduling latency behind GPU execution without explicit pipeline logic.
Chunked prefill tracks extend_prefix_lens to bound memory usage during long-context prompt processing.
Capacity retraction with victim selection (decode-origin first, then oldest epoch) and host snapshotting provides graceful degradation under memory pressure.
Kernel registry uses declarative FormatSignature, capability requirements (vendor, arch, features), and per-family oracles for hardware-aware selection.
SelectionObjective enum (latency, throughput, portability, determinism, debug) provides first-class optimization targets per call site.

candidates.effect: Enforce request lifecycle state transitions via typed finite-state machine with compile-time transition verification.
candidates.outcome: FAK has policy/guard evaluation but lacks a typed state-machine contract for tool-call and session lifecycle transitions.

candidates.effect: Overlap schedule execution by decoupling step planning from result landing using bounded in-flight depth and in-flight tracking.
candidates.outcome: FAK currently executes tool calls sequentially; bounded overlap planning can hide host-side validation latency behind model turns.

candidates.effect: Select execution kernels through declarative capability gating, format signatures, and per-family domain oracles.
candidates.outcome: FAK model registry resolves models procedurally; adopting declarative format signature and capability matching improves multi-backend routing.

candidates.effect: Provide first-class selection objectives (latency, throughput, portability, determinism, debug) to steer execution ranking.
candidates.outcome: FAK routing policies support cost and score but lack explicit first-class optimization objective tags.

candidates.effect: Recover from capacity exhaustion via victim retraction with epoch-ordered readmission and host-backed snapshotting.
candidates.outcome: FAK manages context via ctxmmu but does not implement epoch-ordered victim retraction under multi-session concurrency.

candidates.effect: Coordinate multi-tier KV caches with two-tier prefix probe and asynchronous host streaming.
candidates.outcome: FAK context pager operates on local memory spans; tiered host/device prefix coordination is relevant when scaling local inference.

candidates.effect: Run headless inference scheduler driven directly by external orchestrator over compact binary messaging.
candidates.outcome: FAK provides gateway serve mode but does not export an embeddable headless scheduler protocol for third-party control planes.
